problem: The sentence says 'voting and isolation reduce it further' after the all-lanes-fail probability. Once every lane has failed there is nothing left to vote on or isolate, so this teaches the wrong mechanism. Voting and isolation act before the all-lanes-fail event, not after it.
fix: Voting and isolation stop one failed lane from causing loss of control; the number p^k estimates the loss of all lanes, which is the event compared with the 1 × 10⁻⁹ per hour target. Both answers lie below that target.

problem: 'Digital FBW is not just analog FBW with a computer' is confusing because analog FBW also used a computer. The real difference is sampling and software.
fix: Digital FBW is not just analog FBW with a faster computer: sampling, software validation, built-in test and software gain scheduling are part of the design.

problem: The question asks for two reasons FBL suits fuel tanks, but the answer gives 'no spark hazard' plus 'immunity to EMI and ground loops'. EMI immunity is not a fuel-tank reason; it is a general FBL advantage.
fix: Answer: in a fuel tank, fibre carries no current, so it cannot cause a spark, and it is immune to EMI from nearby wiring and lightning currents. General FBL advantages (no ground loops, light weight, high bandwidth) are separate.

problem: The answer writes 'pk' as plain text, which reads as p times k instead of p to the power k.
fix: Write p<sup>k</sup> (probability that all k independent lanes fail in one hour).

problem: 'dynamic pressure qbar' uses a spelled-out symbol and gives no unit, unlike the other quantities.
fix: Air data gives airspeed V in m/s, dynamic pressure q̄ = ½ρV² in Pa (q is avoided because it already means pitch rate) and angle of attack α in degrees.

problem: The answer says a 'sidestick gradient must create stick force that rises with speed and deflection'. A plain spring gradient in a sidestick does not rise with speed; only Q-feel does.
fix: Q-feel (a force that rises with dynamic pressure) makes stick force grow with speed; the sidestick spring gradient sets the force per unit of stick deflection.
